clue.text: Wasted evening?

parts.note: wasted is slang for very drunk, so an evening spent getting wasted is a drinking session, not a squandered night

explanation.surface: Someone regrets a night that achieved nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' reads as squandered, but here it is slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy drinking party is an evening at which the guests get thoroughly drunk.

clue.text: Got drunk into a bed

indicators.note: a drunk person's movements are jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone, too drunk to stand, managed to get into bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' is the anagram signal working on INTO A BED.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are past tenses meaning acquired or came to have something.

clue.text: Oh! Critical time!

parts.note: the two letters of this exclamation can be read as the symbols for nought and hour: O for zero, H for hour

explanation.surface: An exclamation of alarm as a crucial moment arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer, read as wordplay, would give O (zero) followed by H (hour), which spells 'Oh'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the scheduled moment an operation begins, hence any decisive or critical moment.

clue.text: One going round on his bike?

definitions.text: One going round on his bike?

parts.words: One going round on his bike?
parts.note: suggests a cyclist doing laps, but the One is literal: a rider of a machine with a single wheel

explanation.surface: A cyclist circling about on his bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' hints at the prefix uni-, and the bike has just one wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider of a single-wheeled cycle, often a circus performer pedalling in circles.

clue.text: Constant smoker seen in Vietnam

indicators.note: says the answer can be spotted sitting inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A chain-smoker spotted while travelling in Vietnam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constant smoker' sounds like a person, but it is a volcano that keeps on smoking.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian volcano is almost continuously active, giving off smoke for much of the time.

clue.text: Iron Lady displays top fashion

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
Dora is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher, the Iron Lady, shows off the latest high fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Lady' suggests Thatcher, but it splits into a chemical symbol and a woman's name; 'top' here is a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft felt hat with a creased crown, a style of headwear: top meaning something worn on the head.

clue.text: Judge soldiers about to block charge

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: something put in the middle of a passage blocks it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service
re is Latin-derived for about or concerning

explanation.surface: A court judge sees troops stopping a cavalry charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' suggests an attack by troops, but it is a fee; RE for Royal Engineers is a standard crossword soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports official who rules on play acts as the judge of a match.

clue.text: Big bodies in aircraft on way up

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it, so comes first

parts.note: a plane is an aircraft

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Large people boarding an aircraft as it climbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ST into TS beneath PLANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Worlds such as Jupiter and Saturn are huge celestial bodies orbiting the sun.

clue.text: Region in shade there allows light

indicators.note: Region in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An area of shadow nonetheless lets some light through.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across shadE THERE ALlows.
explanation.definitionFit: Something airy and delicate, as if not of this world, is light in the sense of insubstantial.

clue.text: Controversial body-builder editors slammed

indicators.note: slammed suggests the word editors is battered out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Newspaper editors attacked a controversial bodybuilder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slammed' reads as criticised but signals the anagram of EDITORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Anabolic drugs used to build muscle are a contentious aid to bodybuilding.

clue.text: Ruler on plane sick having eaten duck

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside, so one piece sits within the other
feeling sick, the words on plane are in a disordered state and get rearranged

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A ruler feels airsick on a flight after dining on duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sick' rearranges ON PLANE to NAPLEON, and 'having eaten' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The French emperor Bonaparte was a ruler of France and much of Europe.

clue.text: Last but one in political residence

definitions.meaning: in a cricket batting order of eleven, the batsman going in tenth is the last but one
the British Prime Minister lives at 10 Downing Street

explanation.surface: The second-to-last person inside a politician's home.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket batting orders run from one to eleven, so the tenth man in is last but one.
explanation.definitionFit: Downing Street's tenth house is the PM's official home, and tenth in an eleven-man order is penultimate.

clue.text: Extremely minute number dropping ecstasy

indicators.note: dropping means the letter is let go from the word

parts.note: eighty is a number
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A tiny number of people giving up the drug ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely minute' looks like one phrase meaning tiny, but the definition stops at 'Extremely'.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, the word is an intensifier meaning very, as in 'mighty fine'.

clue.text: Point for me in remark that's smug

indicators.note: one thing in place of another, so the first word swaps in where the second stood

parts.note: a comment is a remark
a point is a particular place or spot

explanation.surface: Someone notices a remark about them that seems self-satisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' looks like a comment's thrust, but it means a spot or location.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe being pleased with oneself and unconcerned about any shortcomings.

clue.text: Golfer playing in Loire event

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of Loire event are tossed about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer competing in a tournament in France's Loire valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' fits the golfer scene but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mexican-American champion won six major championships in professional golf.

clue.text: One loving sound of cello player?

indicators.note: says the word is said aloud rather than written

parts.note: a bow is what plays a cello's strings

explanation.surface: A music lover fond of the tone of a cellist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cello player' looks like a cellist, but it is the bow drawn across the strings, said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A boyfriend or admirer is one who is courting or in love with someone.

clue.text: Gather man will create commotion

parts.note: to raise funds is to gather them
he'll is a contraction of he will, with he standing for a man

explanation.surface: A man warns that gathering people will cause a disturbance.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make an angry uproar or cause a lot of trouble.

clue.text: This should refresh article in French newspaper

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: Le Monde is a leading Paris daily
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A French newspaper article designed to revive readers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cool citrus soft drink is a classic refreshment.

clue.text: Is he in gang or excluded?

indicators.note: the first words go inside the gang's letters

parts.note: a band is a gang or group

explanation.surface: A question whether a man belongs to the gang or has been shut out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sent away or banned from a place means being excluded from it.

clue.text: Turn to hold mug and a tumbler

indicators.note: the outer word holds the others inside it

parts.note: a turn is a performer's act on stage
to mug someone is to rob them

explanation.surface: Someone tries to grip a mug and a drinking glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tumbler' and 'mug' suggest drinking vessels; the tumbler is a gymnast.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast who performs somersaults and flips is a tumbler.

clue.text: Copy one — friend keeps it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the second piece goes within the first

parts.note: a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone tells a friend to keep a copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is taken as written, not as a pronoun for the copy.
explanation.definitionFit: To mimic or reproduce someone's behaviour is to copy them.

clue.text: Northern beer knocked back in style

indicators.note: knocked back reads as drunk down, but here it means the letters run backwards

parts.note: ale is a beer

explanation.surface: A northern beer downed with some flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' suits drinking the beer but turns NALE around.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair and vigorous panache make up a kind of style.

clue.text: Cold changing room accommodates little Parisian rival

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: a host accommodates a guest inside, so one piece goes within the other
changing says the letters of room are altered in order

parts.note: petit is French for little

explanation.surface: A chilly changing room has space for a small French rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing room' looks like a single place, but 'changing' rearranges ROOM to OMOR, which 'accommodates' PETIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor is an opponent in a contest, and so a rival.

clue.text: Tax cut

definitions.meaning: a duty levied on goods produced at home
to remove by cutting out, as a surgeon does

explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a duty on domestic goods, and the verb means to remove surgically.

clue.text: Bizarre old books with one chapter

parts.note: ex- means former or old
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Strange old books, each with only a single chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: Strikingly unusual or foreign things may seem bizarre or outlandish.

clue.text: One to observe pupils very closely

definitions.text: One to observe pupils very closely

parts.words: One to observe pupils very closely
parts.note: suggests a strict teacher watching schoolchildren, but the pupils are the openings at the centre of eyes

explanation.surface: A watchful teacher keeping a close eye on the class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupils' looks like schoolchildren; it means parts of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-care specialist examines people's eyes, including the pupil, at very close range.

clue.text: A riddle that doesn't end? You're joking!

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a riddle is a coarse sieve, so to riddle is to sift

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a riddle with no punchline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riddle' reads as a puzzle but is a sieve; SIFT loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The scornful exclamation expresses disbelief, much as 'you can't be serious!' does.

clue.text: Fish served in pub round country area

indicators.note: the pub's letters go round the country

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house
Iran is a country

explanation.surface: Fish on the menu at a pub somewhere out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served in' is only link padding for the menu picture; PH is the map abbreviation for a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp-toothed South American river species is a predatory fish.

clue.text: Aesthetically pleasing model reversed in lorry

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: artic is British short for an articulated lorry, a big truck

indicators.note: the letters are read backwards

parts.note: to sit for an artist is to model

explanation.surface: A tasteful model is backed into a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: An artic is a British articulated lorry, a large truck with a separate cab.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing good taste or creative skill makes something attractive to the eye.

clue.text: These discarded when drawing finished?

parts.note: suggests an artist's scraps, but the drawing is puffing on a cigarette, and the stubs are thrown away

explanation.surface: Sketches thrown away once an artist completes a drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' means inhaling on a cigarette, not sketching.
explanation.definitionFit: Cigarette butts are the leftover stubs thrown away after the smoke is finished.
